newsitem.title: UK: Blair presses on with Scottsh, Welsh assembly plans.
newsitem.headline: Blair presses on with Scottsh, Welsh assembly plans.

text.p: British Prime Minister Tony Blair on Thursday signalled his determination to push through plans to give Scotland and Wales their own parliaments by scheduling debates on the legislation in the House of Commons next week.

Shortly after Blair's Labour government published a bill to allow for referendums to be held in Scotland and Wales, its parliamentary business manager Ann Taylor announced that the first discussion of it by MPs would take place next Tuesday and Wednesday.
Blair's government plans a Scottish parliament with a limited ability to raise taxes in Edinburgh, and a rather less powerful Welsh Senedd (senate) in Cardiff to take decisions on local issues.
The opposition Conservatives say setting up these bodies could be the first step on a path to the break-up of Britain.

But Conservative threats to obstruct the devolution proposals have been blunted by Labour's landslide election victory on May 1, and the fact that the opposition party now has not a single seat in either Scotland or Wales.
In Scotland, Labour has 56 seats, the minority Liberal Democrats, who also favour devolution, 10 and the pro-independence Scottish National Party six.
The government hopes to hold the referendums in the autumn, and, provided voters approve of the parliaments, to introduce a bill to set them up soon after that.

In 1978, the last Labour government also offered Scotland and Wales their own parliaments. The Welsh decisively rejected the idea and a referendum in Scotland showed only a wafer-thin majority in favour of the idea, which was then dropped.
